title: O Thou Great Friend to All the Sons of Men
description: O Thou Great Friend to All the Sons of Men in Tonic Solfa to ELLERS, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Theodore Parker wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 156, “Christ the Way, the Truth and the Life”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Tens (10.10.10.10), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ELLERS; any other Tens tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Thou great Friend to all the sons of men, Who once ap-peared in hum-blest guise be-low, Sin to re-buke, to break the cap-tive's chain, And call thy bre-thren forth from want and woe;

lines: O Thou great Friend to all the sons of men,
Who once appeared in humblest guise below,
Sin to rebuke, to break the captive's chain,
And call thy brethren forth from want and woe;
We look to thee! thy truth is still the Light,
Which guides the nations, groping on their way,
Stumbling and falling in disastrous night,
Yet hoping ever for the perfect day.
Yes! thou art still the Life; thou art the way
The holiest know; — Light, Life, and Way of heaven!
And they who dearest hope, and deepest pray,
Toil by the light, life, way, which thou hast given.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Theodore Parker died in 1860.
credits: Words by Theodore Parker (1810–1860), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ELLERS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
